title: The Rough Provision
premise: Tamsin Okonkwo, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries for a rescue that went catastrophically wrong, is hired off the books to find a vanished government survey team in the Karveth Range. Following the survey gear upstream, Tamsin discovers the team wasn't lost — they found the river's forbidden source, a glacial vault holding records of a state-sanctioned massacre, and were silenced for it. Hunted by the officials who ruined Tamsin's name years ago, and shadowed by the sole surviving surveyor who may not be trustworthy, Tamsin must choose between selling the evidence to buy back their reputation or releasing it publicly at the cost of everything. In the end, Tamsin broadcasts the truth from the source itself, accepts permanent exile, and finds that loyalty — to the dead, and to one unexpected ally — was worth more than vindication.
about_author: Vesper Eriksen is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade outfitting climbs across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people the maps forgot, drawing on real search-and-rescue archives and a lifelong obsession with rivers that refuse to be named.

chapters.title: The Blacklist Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Broke and unemployable in the border town of Halden's Rest, Tamsin takes a cash job guiding a 'geological consultant' into the Karveth foothills. The beat: weary pragmatism masking old shame over the disaster that got them blacklisted.

chapters.title: Gear With No Owners
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Above the treeline they find an abandoned survey camp — tents pitched, stove warm, radios silent, no tracks leading out. The consultant, Ilse Varga, goes pale and orders them downstream. Beat: creeping dread.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Descending, they find a surveyor's body snagged in a rapids, notebook waterproofed against his chest. Ilse admits she's government intelligence; the team found something upstream. Beat: betrayal reframed as desperate alliance.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In town, Tamsin is cornered by Deputy Minister Corrigan — the man who built their blacklist — offering full reinstatement if they retrieve the survey data quietly. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin refuses and flees with the dead man's notebook, meeting Rook Adeyemi, the survey team's missing fifth member, half-frozen in a cave. Beat: wary trust between two liars.

chapters.title: Rook's Version
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook claims the team split after finding a sealed glacial vault; he ran when their leader talked of going public. His story doesn't quite hold. Beat: suspicion braided with sympathy.

chapters.title: The Compass Bearing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The notebook's final pages contain bearings matching Tamsin's own compass — inherited from the father whose death the massacre records concern. Beat: personal history detonating inside the mission.

chapters.title: Corrigan's Net
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Government trackers seal the valley's exits; a bounty goes out naming Tamsin as the survey killer. Beat: the noose tightening, framed through official documents and radio chatter.

chapters.title: Whiteout Crossing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A storm forces a brutal high-pass crossing; Rook saves Tamsin's life, then is caught confessing he already sold the vault's location once. Beat: loyalty tested and cracked.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A hidden valley community of massacre descendants shelters them, revealing the vault holds their families' testimony, collected for decades. Beat: grief becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Ilse Returns
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse intercepts them, claiming she's gone rogue too — but her radio still transmits. Tamsin must decide whether she's ally or leash. Beat: paranoia sharpened by tenderness.

chapters.title: The First Vault Door
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the glacier's face they find the survey team's drilling rig and fresh blood. Inside the ice: a steel door older than the state itself. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: What Was Buried Twice
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook finally tells the whole truth: he led Corrigan here before, took money, and the team died because of him. Beat: confession as self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Long Descent Trap
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Corrigan's men ambush them at the only safe descent; Ilse turns her radio on deliberately, buying time with her capture. Beat: sacrifice that rewrites every earlier doubt.

chapters.title: Interrogation at Camp Four
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Captured, Ilse stalls Corrigan while learning his plan: melt the vault, destroy the records, blame the villagers. Beat: cold fury under a compliant mask.

chapters.title: The Frozen Testimony
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin and Rook breach the vault via a crevasse route only a blacklisted guide would know. Inside: decades of recorded testimony, including Tamsin's father's voice. Beat: devastating recognition.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Rope
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Rook offers to take the blame publicly so Tamsin can walk free with the records; Tamsin refuses to let another person be erased for them. Beat: loyalty chosen over survival.

chapters.title: Corrigan at the Source
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Corrigan arrives with Ilse as hostage, offering Tamsin the deal again — name cleared, debt paid, silence bought. Beat: the climax of temptation.

chapters.title: Broadcast From the Ice
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Using the vault's old transmitter and the village's satellite phone, they stream the testimony live as Corrigan's men move in. Beat: defiant, breathless climax.

chapters.title: The Glacier Gives Way
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Corrigan tries to destroy the vault; the destabilized ice collapses, taking him and the original door. Tamsin drags Rook from the flood. Beat: cathartic destruction and near-loss.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Weeks later: the recordings are public, the village named, Corrigan's network exposed. Tamsin remains blacklisted — the truth exonerated no one officially. Beat: bittersweet justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Rough Provision
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin guides the village's young people on their first ascent of the source, compass in hand, staying where the maps end. Final beat: exile transformed into belonging; the debt repaid in a new currency.
